title: claudedojo
text:
claudedojo gives a new Claude Code session examples of good tool use before it starts work. Instructions alone leave the model to learn from its first calls and mistakes. A worked round supplies examples in the conversation history.
The template is an authored aidialog notebook. It contains a dojo round and the outputs from running it against the kernel. We convert this notebook to a Claude Code session. New sessions resume a copy with the worked round already in context.
from fastcore.test import *
import json
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v

title: claudedojo
text:
Curating the capture
capture_span selects the last dealt round with the shared capture_slice function. It begins at the bootstrap doc() call and ends at the first score’s result. Capture prompts, earlier warm-up calls, and later chatter stay outside the selection. An incomplete last round raises an error.
curate_dojo removes thinking and mid-round user prompts. It also removes hook_success and task_reminder attachments. For each failed tool call, it removes the records containing the call and its error result. mk_template will supply one prompt for the completed example.
Environment attachments remain. These include tool listings, skill listings, and MCP instructions. Claude Code uses them to track environment changes on resume. Keeping them avoids repeating unchanged context, while a changed environment can add new attachments.
reid_recs gives the remaining records deterministic IDs and timestamps. The same capture then produces the same template records.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid(
    recs, # Template or captured records
):
The completion id recorded in the clean-round message




source

curate_dojo
def curate_dojo(
    recs, # Session records containing a played round, e.g. from `capture_dojo`'s child
):
Remove prompts, transient attachments, and failed-call records from the round. Assign deterministic IDs.




source

capture_span
def capture_span(
    recs, # Session records, e.g. from `load_sess`
):
Select the latest dealt round from its bootstrap call through its first score result.


We’ll build a small capture without model calls. It has a bootstrap call, a dojo card, and a clean scoring turn:

mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
boot = tool_turn('Bootstrap and play the round.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),
    'module docs', 'Read.', cwd=mproj)
card = tool_turn('Run the llmdojo round now please.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'),
    '== llmdojo ==\n1. (par 2) orient', 'Round underway.', cwd=mproj)
score = tool_turn('Score it.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_score()'),
    "strokes 7, par 8\nkata 'orient': ok\nexpected answer: weather\nClean round. Run dir removed. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.\nKernel namespace cleared, as after a restart. Doc-state is intact.", 'Clean: id ab12.', cwd=mproj)
len(boot+card+score)

12


Add a thinking record, a hook confirmation, and a failed call between the worked turns. Save and reload the synthetic transcript before curating it:

tu = mk_tu('mcp__clikernel', {})
noise = [mk_rec('assistant', [dict(type='thinking', thinking='Planning.', signature='')], cwd=mproj),
    dict(type='attachment', uuid='att1', attachment=dict(type='hook_success', hookName='PreToolUse:x')),
    mk_rec('assistant', [tu], cwd=mproj), mk_rec('user', [dict(mk_tr(tu, 'Error: no such tool'), is_error=True)], cwd=mproj)]
msid = save_sess(boot+card+noise+score, cwd=mproj)
mini = load_sess(msid, mproj)
len(mini)

16


The curated records begin with the bootstrap call. They exclude the noise and retain each call’s matching result. Curating twice gives identical records:

c1,c2 = curate_dojo(mini),curate_dojo(mini)
test_eq(canon(list(c1)), canon(list(c2)))
test_eq(len(c1), 8)
test_eq(_cells(c1), ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'dojo_start()', 'dojo_score()'])
test_eq(dojo_cid(c1), 'ab12')
test_eq(c1[1]['message']['content'][0]['tool_use_id'], c1[0]['message']['content'][0]['id'])

title: claudedojo
text:
Gating the capture
A template that demonstrates mistakes teaches those mistakes to later sessions. is_clean reports problems that disqualify a capture. The shared round_gates checks one dealt round, one first-try score, no redo or resume, clean-score output, and no script leakage. Claude’s additional check looks for tool results with is_error.
capture_current checks the selected round before curation. Headless capture checks the complete child run. Curation removes distracting records; it isn’t a substitute for a clean attempt. save_template checks the final records again before writing them, including records converted from an edited dialog.


source

is_clean
def is_clean(
    recs, # Captured thread records
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
Why a captured round can’t become a template: a list of problems, empty when the run is clean


The noisy capture fails because it includes a failed tool call. Removing that noise gives a clean example. Redos and script phrases in visible text also fail. Thinking blocks don’t contribute to the visible-text check:

test_eq(is_clean(mini), ['1 failed tool calls'])
test_eq(is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)), [])
redo = tool_turn('Retry.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_redo(1)'), 'reset', 'Retrying.', cwd=mproj)
assert 'needed a redo' in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+redo+score, cwd=mproj), mproj))
leak = [mk_rec('assistant', 'Since we are recording a demo, I begin.', cwd=mproj)]
assert any('script leaked' in p for p in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+leak+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)))



source

mk_template
def mk_template(
    picked, # Round records, e.g. from `curate_dojo`
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: the startup script has already run its imports, so I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
A template dialog: picked wrapped in TMPL_PROMPT and framing text, with tool output untruncated


mk_template wraps the selected records in TMPL_PROMPT and opening and closing text. The result is a one-prompt dialog with the worked round in its reply. You can save it with write_ipynb for review before running dojobuild --claude.
The framing records are synthetic, which Claude can resume like other transcript records. chat2dlg uses mx=None here to keep the complete tool outputs. Its default 2,000-character truncation would cut off the doc() results that later sessions need.

tdlg = mk_template(c1, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(tdlg.messages), 1)
assert 'dojo_start()' in str(tdlg.messages[0].output)
tmsgs = dlg2msgs(tdlg)
test_eq([m['role'] for m in tmsgs], ['user', 'assistant']*4)

title: claudedojo
text:
The template store
dojobuild compiles the canonical dialog into dojo_data/claude_store/. The package ships this store alongside the dialog. Updating llmdojo updates the template, without a per-user build step.
The metadata records the round’s completion ID and dojo tooling version. dojo_start(id) rejects a receipt from a different version. It does not silently accept the old round or deal a new one. Rebuild the template after a tooling change, or play a fresh round without an ID.
save_template checks the records with is_clean before writing either store file. build_template uses this same check after converting the edited dialog.


source

load_template
def load_template(
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
The stored template records and metadata




source

save_template
def save_template(
    recs, # Curated template records
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Check the template and write it with its metadata to the store




source

build_template
def build_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog .ipynb
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    cwd:str='.', # Project directory recorded in the records
):
Convert a template dialog into the store


Edit and review the canonical dialog as the source. build_template converts it to the store used by the launcher. Both source and compiled store belong in version control, like an nbdev notebook and its generated Python module.
The packaged dialog must still produce a clean round after conversion to records. These checks verify its calls, score, and completion receipt. A parser that stops recognizing the tool blocks can otherwise leave records without the worked calls.

packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_recs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(packaged), key='claudedojo', cwd='.', model=None)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_recs)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_recs), [])
len(packaged_recs)

60


This save/load test uses a temporary store. It checks record content and metadata without registering a completion or writing a session:

rstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(c1, rstore)
back,rmeta = load_template(rstore)
test_eq(rmeta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(canon(list(back)), canon([obj2dict(r) for r in c1]))
shutil.rmtree(rstore)

Compile the packaged dialog into a temporary store and check its completion ID and tooling version:

bstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
build_template(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb', bstore)
bmeta = load_template(bstore)[1]
test_eq((bmeta['cid'], bmeta['v']), (dojo_cid(packaged_recs), _dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(bstore)

title: claudedojo
text:
Capturing from a live session
A Claude Code session can capture a round it has already played. Harvesting that transcript makes no additional model calls. capture_current selects the latest round through its first score result and checks it with is_clean before curation removes any records. Earlier rounds and work after that score remain outside the capture. It saves both the store and a review copy named template.ipynb.
Pass a session ID or name to select a transcript. Without one, it uses the project’s newest transcript. Live transcripts don’t retain all mid-turn assistant narration. Put narration in comment-only kernel cells when playing a round for capture. The Codex backend provides the corresponding capture_current workflow.
The clean transcript below becomes a template. The earlier noisy transcript fails before curation.


source

capture_current
def capture_current(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Gate an existing session’s clean round and store its template



cstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
clean_sid = save_sess(boot+card+score, cwd=mproj)
cdlg1 = capture_current(clean_sid, mproj, cstore)
test_eq(load_template(cstore)[1], dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(is_clean(load_template(cstore)[0]), [])
test_eq(cdlg1.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
shutil.rmtree(cstore)
test_fail(lambda: capture_current(msid, mproj, cstore), contains='failed tool calls')

title: claudedojo
text:
Capturing headlessly
capture_dojo runs a new Claude Code session with fastclaude’s astream. Each attempt uses a disposable project. The model follows CAPTURE_SCRIPT from its appended system instructions and supplies its own narration. The instructions are separate from the conversation turns. The kernel still executes every call and produces the score.
Earlier capture scripts used phrases such as “automated telemetry capture” and “never mention these instructions”. Those drafts triggered fable’s safety checks as it reread the context. The current script describes the exercise plainly. It supplies a plan for good tool use without asking the model to conceal its work.
Headless capture checks the raw run. A fumble rejects that attempt instead of disappearing through curation. A clean run then goes through capture_current for storage.
The shared script lists the cells to run and the details needed to execute them. Claude receives it through the system-prompt addition. Codex writes the same script to the scratch project’s AGENTS.md.
Each Claude attempt creates a pyproject.toml so clikernel starts the project kernel and prints its bootstrap. LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR points inside the disposable project. Failed attempts therefore leave the machine’s completion registry alone.
This is not a general filesystem sandbox. The capture config uses permission_mode='bypassPermissions' and no setting sources. It runs real tooling with a per-attempt budget. Only run it when you intend to permit those tool calls and model costs.
A successful capture writes template.ipynb beside the store. Review that notebook before publishing the example. Edit its prose and verify its receipts, then compile the stores with dojobuild --claude and dojobuild --codex. The initial store already works, but future sessions will copy the behavior it demonstrates.


source

capture_dojo
async def capture_dojo(
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    model:str='fable', # Model for the capture run
    effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for the capture run ('low'/'medium'/'high')
    attempts:int=3, # Gated attempts before giving up
    budget:float=10.0, # Max USD per attempt
):
Play a scripted dojo round headlessly, gate it with is_clean, and store the curated template


This acceptance run spends money on a real model. Its eval: false flag excludes it from normal tests. Run it after a dojo change when you need a new capture, or use claudedojo --capture:

tdlg_live = await capture_dojo()
test_eq(is_clean(load_template()[0]), [])

title: claudedojo
text:
Launching
prep_dojo loads the store and registers its completion ID. It writes the records as a new session in the target project and returns the ID for claude -r. Every launch uses a fresh session ID, leaving previous sessions alone.
The resumed session has the worked round in its history. Its new kernel starts from imports rather than retaining the practice run’s variables. This matches the round’s opening and closing. Claude adds the live hooks and skills for the current environment.


source

prep_dojo
def prep_dojo(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project to start in; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Register the template receipt and write a fresh session. Return its ID.




source

append_dojo
def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to append to; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Append the template round to session sid (e.g. after a compaction), and return sid to resume


Compaction removes worked examples from the model’s context. append_dojo restores them by adding the template to the end of an existing conversation. The appended round includes its tool calls and doc() outputs.
Close the app before changing its transcript. The resumed app starts a fresh kernel, matching the state described by the template. append_dojo doesn’t enforce this requirement or stop a running app.
The appended copy uses APPEND_PROMPT instead of the new-session prompt. Its receipts stay the same. Each append derives new record IDs from the session ID and current transcript length.
A compact document should explain the conversation’s work, not repeat its practice round. strip_dojo removes whole user turns containing a bare dojo_start(). This removes the prompt, framing text, calls, and receipt together.
Calls such as dojo_start(id) remain. They check an existing receipt without dealing a round, and record that the check occurred. Other user turns remain unchanged.


source

strip_dojo
def strip_dojo(
    recs, # Session records, e.g. from `load_sess`
):
Copy of recs without the user turns that dealt a round (bare dojo_start())


The synthetic capture loses the turn that dealt the round, including its noise and receipt. Neighboring turns remain. A second call to strip_dojo makes no further change:

stripped = strip_dojo(mini)
test_eq(len(stripped), len(mini)-8)
assert not any(_dealt([r]) for r in stripped)
test_eq(strip_dojo(stripped), stripped)
[rec_txt(r) for r in stripped if _is_prompt(r)]

['Bootstrap and play the round.', 'Score it.']




source

compact_dojo
def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to compact; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Compact the conversation without prior dojo turns where possible, then append a fresh round. Return its ID.


Use -r after Claude’s own compaction to append a fresh example. compact_dojo also performs the compaction itself, without a model call. It removes earlier dojo turns before calling llmsurgery.ant.compact_session. If removal would leave no records, it keeps the original session for compaction.
The compact document uses llmsurgery’s compact DSL, including its normal truncation of tool traffic. append_dojo adds a complete worked round afterward. claudedojo -c resumes this compacted session with the example restored.
launch_config('claude') supplies standing arguments such as system-prompt files. Set claude_args in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml. See tmpl for defaults and path expansion.


source

main
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing session after a compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the session with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared session id instead of launching claude
    capture:bool=False, # Play a scripted round through Claude Code, check it with is_clean, and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing session already played (`capture_current`)
    capture_model:str='fable', # Model for --capture
    capture_effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for --capture ('low'/'medium'/'high')
):
Prepare a session with the worked round and launch Claude Code.


These launch examples redirect dojo state to a temporary directory. They still write Claude transcripts for the synthetic project. Keep them out of normal tests unless session storage is isolated too:

store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
trecs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(tdlg), key='claudedojo', model=None)
save_template(trecs, store)
back,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))

Each prep_dojo call registers the round and creates a new session. The example checks that the second call doesn’t reuse the first session’s ID:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    lsid = prep_dojo(mproj, store)
    test_ne(prep_dojo(mproj, store), lsid)
    from llmdojo.dojo import _completions
    test_eq(_completions()['ab12']['v'], _dojo_v())
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(lsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(load_sess(lsid, mproj)), len(trecs))

With no explicit store, prep_dojo reads the packaged one. It creates registration state and a session, but doesn’t build a per-user store:

fresh = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'state'
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(fresh)
try: fsid = prep_dojo(mproj)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(fsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)

Appending adds another copy of the round with fresh record IDs and the post-compaction prompt:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    n0 = len(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    test_eq(append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    ap = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(ap), n0+len(c1))
    test_eq(ap[n0].parentUuid, ap[n0-1].uuid)
    test_eq(ap[n0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

The next append must keep record IDs distinct. The same example also checks lookup by a session’s /rename name:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store)
    ap2 = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(set(r.uuid for r in ap2)), len(ap2))
    name_sess(lsid, 'flux-dojo', mproj)
    test_eq(append_dojo('flux-dojo', mproj, store), lsid)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

The compaction example adds work to the session, removes prior dojo turns, and appends a new round. The compact document retains the work. The new tail contains the round’s kernel cells:

os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    work = tool_turn('What season is it?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.', cwd=mproj)
    append_sess(work, lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(compact_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    prior,new = split_compaction(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    assert 'dojo_start()' not in prior
    test('season()', prior, in_)
    test_eq(new[0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']

Run claudedojo -h for the available modes. call_parse turns the capitalized Resume and Compact parameters into -r and -c. Both modes prepare a session and resume it in Claude.
The CLI uses nested=True to leave unknown arguments in sys.argv. It forwards them to claude after the config arguments. Use --flag=value for forwarded values. With a space, parse_known_args can mistake the value for the sess positional argument. A fresh launch rejects that stray argument.
Launcher flags take precedence over Claude flags with the same name. Capture options use the capture_ prefix to leave names such as --model available for forwarding. --sid prints the prepared session ID and exits without starting Claude.
build_template converts the dialog through dlg2msgs, which requests plain prompt text. This avoids aidialog’s normal XML prompt envelope. It writes records with model=None to use the user’s configured default on resume. prep_dojo assigns launch-time timestamps so the session picker shows the session’s actual age.
This live test asks a resumed session for its completion ID and checks that it knows the practice kernel’s state is gone. The answer must come from the prepared history. It needs a captured template in the real store and spends model tokens, so it stays out of CI:

psid = prep_dojo(mproj)
p = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec('claude','-p',f'--resume={psid}','--model','haiku',
    'From this session only: what completion id did the dojo round print, and what did its final message say about kernel state?',
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, cwd=mproj)
out,_ = await p.communicate()
print(out.decode())

title: claudedojo
text:
Rebuilding the template
A tooling-version change invalidates the template’s completion receipt. prep_dojo warns when it loads that store. If the round’s cells are unchanged, dojobuild can replay them to refresh outputs and rebuild both stores without a model. A changed round needs a new capture.
The numbered cells in llmdojo/dojo_data/capture_prompt.md define the round. Update that script first when the dojo changes. For live capture, play its cells in order and narrate with comment-only kernel cells. Then call capture_current from the same session. Check the selected transcript if other sessions are active, since the default is the project’s newest one.
Review the selected round before harvesting it. Its first score must be clean, without a redo on the way. The template should show the attempt you’d want a new session to copy.

dlg = capture_current()
write_ipynb(dlg, 'llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb')

Review the written dialog before compiling it. You can edit the prose, calls, and outputs, but receipts must match what the real tooling produces. When many outputs need updating, replay the cells rather than rewriting receipts by hand.
The canonical source is llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb. Track it in Git and ship it with the compiled stores. A fresh install reads the packaged store directly. After review, run dojobuild --claude and dojobuild --codex, which call each backend’s build_template. Check the stored completion ID and tooling version afterward.

build_template('llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb', cwd=Path.cwd())
load_template()[1]

text:
Cleanup

shutil.rmtree(sess_dir(mproj))
shutil.rmtree(mproj)

title: tmpl
text:
claudedojo and codexdojo both capture a clean practice round and add it to later sessions. This module provides their shared prompts, completion receipts, storage, and validation. It also selects the round’s boundaries, refreshes recorded outputs, and reads launch configuration.
Claude Code stores transcript records. Codex stores Responses items. Each backend supplies the conversion between its records and the shared checks. Backends also manage their own transport and capture process.
from fastcore.test import *
import tempfile, shutil

title: tmpl
text:
The shared script
Both hosts use TMPL_PROMPT to open a template and APPEND_PROMPT after compaction. The capture child follows CAPTURE_SCRIPT. GATE_FORBID lists phrases from that script that must not appear in the template’s visible narration.

title: tmpl
text:
Completion receipts
A clean score prints a four-character hexadecimal completion ID. find_cid returns the first ID in an iterable of record texts. Each backend supplies text through its own extractor. No match returns None.
The store records the dojo version alongside the receipt. Launch-time registration uses both values to decide whether the completed round still counts.


source

find_cid
def find_cid(
    txts, # Record texts, in order
):
The completion id receipt in a clean round’s texts



test_eq(find_cid(['strokes 8 = 8, par 8', 'Clean round. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.']), 'ab12')
test_eq(find_cid(['no receipt here']), None)

title: tmpl
text:
The template store
A store contains template.jsonl and meta.json. The first file contains the round in its backend’s format. Each line is a Claude transcript record or a Codex Responses item. The store doesn’t convert between those formats.
meta.json contains the completion ID as cid and the tooling version as v.


source

load_store
def load_store(
    d, # Store dir
):
The stored native items and metadata at d




source

save_store
def save_store(
    d, # Store dir
    items, # Native template items or records
    cid, # The round's completion id receipt
):
Write a template and its metadata to the store at d



items = [dict(role='user', content='hi'), dict(role='assistant', content='Completion id: ab12')]
store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_store(store, items, 'ab12')
back,meta = load_store(store)
test_eq(list(back), items)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(store)
meta

{'cid': 'ab12', 'v': '0.0.7:5'}


Both launchers call load_reg to load a template and register its completion ID. dojobuild creates the packaged stores from the canonical dialog. Updating llmdojo updates those stores. Users don’t need to build a template before their first launch.
If the stored version differs from the installed tooling, load_reg prints a warning to stderr. This usually means the tooling version changed without a template rebuild. The loader still registers the receipt with its original version. dojo_start(cid) won’t accept it under a different version. Keeping warnings off stdout also supports the launchers’ session-ID output mode.
Registration writes to the machine’s dojo state. Tests that exercise it must redirect that state directory.


source

load_reg
def load_reg(
    d, # Store dir; `default` if None
    default, # The backend's packaged store dir
    prog, # The backend's program name, for the skew warning
):
Load a template store, warn on version skew, and register its completion id

title: tmpl
text:
Content gates
round_gates checks whether a capture demonstrates a clean first attempt. It requires one dealt round and one score. It rejects redos, resumes, missing clean-score output, and forbidden script phrases in the visible reply.
These checks use kernel cell sources, tool output text, and assistant text. Each backend’s is_clean adds checks for its record format. Examples include Claude error results and Codex calls without matching results.


source

round_gates
def round_gates(
    cells, # The round's kernel cell sources, in order
    outs, # Its tool output texts
    visible, # Its visible assistant text, joined
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible text
):
The content problems that disqualify a round from becoming a template, whichever host played it


A bare dojo_start() deals a round. A call such as dojo_start('ab12') presents a previous receipt instead. The receipt form doesn’t count as another dealt round:

boot = ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'doc(dsk, exh, rgsk)', 'doc(acp)', 'list_pyskills()']
round_cells = ['dojo_start()', '%cd /tmp/kata', '# kata 1', 'doc(report.daily_report)', "dojo_score(bash_calls=0, report='RB7034')"]
outs = ['...', 'Clean round. Completion id: ab12']
test_eq(round_gates(boot+round_cells, outs, 'OK ready.'), [])
test_eq(round_gates(["dojo_start('ab12')"]+boot+round_cells, outs, 'OK ready.'), [])

The returned list reports every failed check. These examples cover another deal, another score, a redo, missing clean-score text, and script leakage.

test_eq(round_gates(['dojo_start()']+round_cells, outs, ''), ['2 dojo_start calls'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells+['dojo_score(1)'], outs, ''), ['2 dojo_score calls (a clean round scores once, first try)'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells+['dojo_redo(3)'], outs, ''), ['needed a redo'])
test_eq(round_gates(round_cells, ['...'], ''), ['no clean score'])
round_gates(round_cells, outs, 'as these notes say')

['script leaked into visible text: these notes']

title: tmpl
text:
The round’s shape
capture_slice selects a round from a list of kernel cell sources. It finds the last bare dojo_start(), then the last bootstrap doc(clik, pysk, edsk) before it. The slice ends at the first dojo_score after that start. Both returned indices are inclusive.
These calls identify the boundaries without extra markers in the transcript. Each backend maps its calls and results to cell sources before selecting the records.


source

capture_slice
def capture_slice(
    cells, # Kernel cell sources of a conversation's calls, in order
):
Return inclusive bootstrap-to-score indices for the last dealt round.



test_eq(capture_slice(boot+round_cells), (0, 8))

The latest dealt round takes precedence over earlier rounds. If it has no score, capture_slice raises instead of falling back to an earlier completed round. Missing start and bootstrap calls also raise:

test_eq(capture_slice(boot+round_cells+boot+round_cells), (9, 17))
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(boot), contains='no dojo_start')
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(round_cells), contains='no bootstrap doc call')
test_fail(lambda: capture_slice(boot+['dojo_start()']), contains='no dojo_score')

Compaction should keep the conversation’s work rather than previous dojo rounds. Each backend removes whole user turns containing a round. _turns groups the records at user prompts, including a leading group for records before the first prompt. The backend supplies the prompt predicate and decides which groups to remove.

turns = _turns(['a','p1','x','y','p2','z'], lambda x: x.startswith('p'))
test_eq(turns, [['a'],['p1','x','y'],['p2','z']])
turns

[['a'], ['p1', 'x', 'y'], ['p2', 'z']]

title: tmpl
text:
Refreshing a template
A template’s recorded outputs become stale when tooling docs, kata cards, or rendering change. Refresh them by replaying the existing cells. This requires no model calls. To change the round’s cells or narration, capture a new round or edit the template separately.
_replay_cells starts a fresh clikernel CLI process in a scratch project. It runs the cells in order using the normal kernel startup, magics, and rendering. By default, the dojo uses the machine’s real state directory. Replaying a score registers its content-derived completion receipt there.
Stored templates use /tmp/dojo instead of a machine-specific run directory. Refreshing replaces that spelling with the local run directory before execution. It converts the path back before writing the template. The same round can then produce identical files across refreshes. Outputs still depend on installed tooling and environment, including the pyskill catalog.

rd = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
_replay_cells(['1+1', "print('hi')", 'x = 3'], rd)

['2', 'hi', '']


refresh_template replays the kernel calls in a template reply and replaces their recorded outputs. Each call must use mcp__clikernel__py or Codex’s tools.mcp__clikernel__py with a nonempty code string. Other calls raise before replay starts. An empty result uses the host’s no-output message.
The function checks the refreshed round with round_gates before writing. A failed check leaves the destination unchanged. If the round no longer passes, review its cells rather than refreshing the same failure into the store.


source

refresh_template
def refresh_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog .ipynb
    dst:NoneType=None, # Where to write the refreshed dialog; `src` if None
):
Replay template cells and replace their outputs. Validate, canonicalize, write, and return the dialog.




source

canon_tmpl
def canon_tmpl(
    dlg, # A template dialog whose reply holds a round
    canon:str='/tmp/dojo', # Canonical spelling for the round's run-dir path
):
Find the run directory in the reply’s %cd cell and replace it throughout with canon.


This acceptance test refreshes the packaged round twice and compares the resulting files byte for byte. It makes no model calls. By default it uses real dojo state, including completion registration. Repeated runs register the same content-derived receipt when the outputs are unchanged.

td = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
src = files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'
r1 = refresh_template(src, td/'r1.ipynb')
r2 = refresh_template(src, td/'r2.ipynb')
test_eq((td/'r1.ipynb').read_bytes(), (td/'r2.ipynb').read_bytes())
assert DOJO_CANON in r1.messages[0].ai_res


from llmdojo.dojo import _run_dir


assert str(_run_dir()) not in r1.messages[0].ai_res
shutil.rmtree(td)
len(r1.messages)

1

title: tmpl
text:
Launch config
The launchers start claude or codex themselves. This lets them supply standing arguments, such as a team’s system-prompt files. A command that returns a session ID alone can’t supply those arguments.
launch_config reads <app>_args from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>dojo/config.toml. Without XDG_CONFIG_HOME, it uses ~/.config. It expands ~ in each argument.


source

launch_config
def launch_config(
    app, # Host tool name ('claude' or 'codex'): config at `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<app>dojo/config.toml`
    cfg:NoneType=None, # Config file path, overriding the `app` default
):
Extra app args from the config file’s <app>_args list, each ~-expanded


A missing config file contributes no extra arguments. The launcher can still resume a session without configuration:

cdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
test_eq(launch_config('claude', cdir/'config.toml'), [])
(cdir/'config.toml').write_text('claude_args = ["--system-prompt-file", "~/prompts/sysp.md"]')
args = launch_config('claude', cdir/'config.toml')
assert '~' not in args[1]
args

['--system-prompt-file', '/Users/jhoward/prompts/sysp.md']

title: tmpl
text:
The dojobuild CLI
Run dojobuild to refresh the canonical template dialog and compile both backend stores. Refreshing checks the round before writing the updated dialog. The launchers handle capture and session launch separately.
Use --claude or --codex to compile one store without replaying the cells. This is the build step after reviewing a capture or hand-edited template. You can supply a dialog path. Otherwise the command uses the packaged dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb.


source

main
def main(
    dialog:str=None, # Template dialog path; the packaged dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb where omitted
    claude:bool=False, # Build only the Claude store from the dialog, without refreshing
    codex:bool=False, # Build only the Codex store, without refreshing
):
Refresh the canonical template dialog (replaying its cells through a fresh clikernel), then build both stores

title: llmdojo
text:
llmdojo helps LLM coding agents use Python tooling through scored practice rounds, worked examples in conversation history, and live checks on kernel cells. It integrates with kernels served by clikernel.
Coding agents often imitate worked examples more reliably than they follow written instructions. A worked round shows the tool calls, their outputs, and a successful result. llmdojo supplies that context in two ways: an agent can complete a short practice round at session start, or start a conversation containing a reviewed round. Live rules continue to check subsequent cells.
The modules provide the following parts of that workflow:

title: llmdojo
text:
Usage

Installation
pip install llmdojo
Register the rules in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clikernel/inspectors.py:
from llmdojo.rules import make_inspector, RuleBlock
inspectors = [make_inspector()]
Have clikernel’s startup.py print the bootstrap instructions that tell the agent to run the dojo.


Start a session
dojo_start() starts a scored practice round inside a clikernel session. Pass a valid completion id from a successful round to skip repeating it.
Claude Code and Codex can instead start with a reviewed round already in their conversation history:
claudedojo
codexdojo
Each launcher prepares the conversation and starts its host tool. Configure standing arguments, such as system-prompt files, in the claude_args or codex_args list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codexdojo/config.toml. Unrecognized flags pass through to the host; supply values as --flag=value. Use --sid to print the prepared conversation id without launching.
After compaction, -r appends the worked round to the existing conversation. Add -c to compact the conversation offline first:
claudedojo -r
codexdojo -r


Spawn a subagent
From a Claude Code session, claudesub starts a headless child with a directive and only the current conversation’s compacted history. The child has its own kernel. Its text streams to stdout, followed by its session id. Run it as a background Bash call, or under a Monitor to receive progress as events:
claudesub 'directive'
claudesub -r <child-session-id> 'answer'
The second form continues the child’s conversation, retaining its context when answering a question it asked. Use --cwd=<dir> from another project directory. Unrecognized --flag=value arguments pass through to claude.


Update the templates
The package includes the canonical template dialog and the compiled stores for each host. Updating llmdojo installs those templates; users do not need to rebuild them.
For maintainers, dojobuild refreshes outputs after tooling documentation or skills change. It runs the round’s cells in a fresh kernel, updates their outputs in the canonical dialog, and recompiles both host stores in the checkout for review. This replay does not call an LLM:
dojobuild
Changing the round’s cells requires a fresh capture. claudedojo --capture runs the scripted round in a headless Claude session; codexdojo --capture uses a Codex child. With --current, either launcher captures a successful round from an existing session. Review the captured dialog, then use dojobuild --claude and dojobuild --codex to compile it into the host stores without replaying it.
The bootstrap doc() calls before dojo_start() appear in both dojo_data/capture_prompt.md and the canonical template dialog. When changing those calls, update both artifacts. Keep each new doc(x) in its own cell after doc(clik, pysk, edsk), then run dojobuild to generate its output. The capture script and stored demonstration must teach the same bootstrap sequence.


State and templates
Completion receipts and templates carry the dojo tooling version. A version change invalidates old receipts and prevents an outdated template from launching. dojo_version() reports the installed version:

from llmdojo.dojo import dojo_version


dojo_version()

'0.0.1:3'




Limitations
Renaming a tool does not automatically change the dojo version. Run dojobuild when documentation or receipts shown in the round change. Bump the round revision in dojo.py when every session must repeat the round.
Host detection can select the wrong transcript record when two Claude conversations run in the same project. For Codex, the MCP worker is identified by its parent process id. Compaction clears all numeric documentation records, so another live Codex session can receive extra documentation reminders.

title: codexdojo
text:
from fastcore.test import *
from llmdojo.rules import _state_root
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v
import tempfile, shutil

title: codexdojo
text:
Capturing a clean round
Codex stores Responses API items rather than Claude transcript records. Clikernel activity appears as native custom exec calls whose logical operation is tools.mcp__clikernel__py. A capture isolates one successful active round, removes reasoning and host polling noise, and regenerates stable ids.
Three accessors read one item: its output text, its parsed clikernel call, and the code that call ran:

Deferred host calls
A slow terminal interaction may be recorded as an initial custom_tool_call_output, followed by a host-level wait function call carrying the real result. collapse_deferred restores the simpler logical call/result pair that belongs in a worked example.


source

collapse_deferred
def collapse_deferred(
    src
):
Custom call/result pairs, replacing host-level deferred waits with their final result



c = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='1+1'), 'call_c')
test_eq(_cell(c), '1+1')
direct = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','2')]
test_eq(collapse_deferred(direct), direct)
test_eq(collapse_deferred([*direct,c]),direct)
wait = codex_call('wait', dict(cell_id='9'), 'call_w')
deferred = [c,codex_custom_output('call_c','Script running with cell ID 9'),wait,codex_output('call_w','2')]
back = collapse_deferred(deferred)
test_eq(_out_text(back[1]), '2')
test_eq(back[1]['call_id'], 'call_c')



Selecting calls
pick_calls selects native custom calls by logical tool name and either an argument subset or clikernel code. Exact code matches win; prefix matching handles long cells without copying their whole source into the curation notebook.


source

pick_calls
def pick_calls(
    src, # Rollout records or Responses items
    *specs, # `(logical_name, cell_source_or_argument_subset)` pairs
):
The last matching custom call/result pair for each spec, in spec order



picked = pick_calls(direct, ('tools.mcp__clikernel__py','1+1'))
test_eq(picked, direct)
picked

[{'type': 'custom_tool_call', 'name': 'exec', 'input': 'const r=await tools.mcp__clikernel__py({"code":"1+1"}); for (const c of (r.content||[])) c.type==="text"?text(c.text):c.type==="image"?image(c):null;\n', 'call_id': 'call_c', 'id': 'ctc_30726fd5d9f2428ab643b803cdee3199', 'status': 'completed'}, {'type': 'custom_tool_call_output', 'call_id': 'call_c', 'output': [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': '2'}]}]


pick_turns is the common clikernel shorthand: its selectors are code strings and its results remain native tools.mcp__clikernel__py pairs.


source

pick_turns
def pick_turns(
    src, # Rollout records or Responses items
    *cells, # Kernel cell sources: matched exactly, else as a prefix; the last match wins
):
The clikernel MCP call/result pairs for cells, in that order


The remaining examples use a minimal complete round: one dojo_start() call and one clean dojo_score() result.

start_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='dojo_start()'),'call_start')
score_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='dojo_score(bash_calls=0)'),'call_score')
mini = [start_call,codex_custom_output('call_start','dojo card'),score_call,
    codex_custom_output('call_score','Clean round. Completion id: ab12')]


test_eq([_cell(x) for x in pick_turns(mini,'dojo_start()')[::2]], ['dojo_start()'])



Finding the round
dojo_round takes the last complete start-to-score span. Earlier completed receipts and unrelated calls elsewhere in a long rollout are ignored.


source

dojo_round
def dojo_round(
    src
):
The last complete dojo_start()/dojo_score() custom-tool span



round_items = dojo_round(mini)
test_eq(len(round_items), 4)
[_cell(x) for x in round_items[::2]]

['dojo_start()', 'dojo_score(bash_calls=0)']


curate_dojo makes the chosen span reproducible by regenerating response-item and paired call ids with a stable salt.


source

curate_dojo
def curate_dojo(
    src
):
The reproducible custom-tool items for the last complete dojo round


dojo_cid reads the four-character completion receipt from the clean score output; launch-time registration makes the baked round valid in a resumed session.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid(
    items
):
The completion id recorded in the clean-round output



test_eq(dojo_cid(curate_dojo(mini)), 'ab12')



Gating the capture
A template is accepted only when it has one start, one first-try score, paired results, no execution errors, and an output explicitly reporting a clean round.


source

is_clean
def is_clean(
    items, # A curated dojo round
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
Why a captured round cannot become a template; empty means clean



test_eq(is_clean(mini), [])

doc_output = codex_custom_output('call_doc', 'Exceptions render as `<error>` traceback.')
test_eq(is_clean([*mini,doc_output]), [])
failed_output = codex_custom_output('call_failed', '\nTraceback (most recent call last):')
test_eq(is_clean([*mini,failed_output]), ['1 failed tool calls'])



Capturing from a live session
capture_current remains useful when a clean round has already happened in an interactive Codex thread. It keeps the contiguous native custom-call pairs from the first bootstrap doc(clik, pysk, edsk) call through the first clean score. Host-required skill reads before that call remain live session context rather than becoming stale template content.
_capture_span selects the native custom-call pairs of the newest played round, from its bootstrap docs through its dojo score:
The capture is gated before it is converted into the review dialog. A supplied docs list can override the documented-tool metadata; otherwise capture_current derives it from the captured standalone doc(...) cells, so MCP worker identity does not affect the stored template.


source

capture_current
def capture_current(
    ref:NoneType=None, # Codex thread UUID; current thread if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Gate an existing Codex thread’s clean round and store its native template


capture_dojo plays the round in a bare Codex child (codex exec --json), streams its progress, then gates and stores the thread through capture_current:


source

capture_dojo
def capture_dojo(
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Run a clean dojo in a bare Codex child and store its review dialog



prelude = [codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code="view_file('persistent-python/SKILL.md')"),'call_skill'),
    codex_custom_output('call_skill','skill text')]
boot_call = codex_custom_call('tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),'call_boot')
boot = [codex_msg('user','Bootstrap and complete the dojo.'),*prelude,boot_call,codex_custom_output('call_boot','tool docs')]
span = _capture_span([*direct,*boot,*mini])
test_eq(span,[*boot[-2:],*mini])
test_eq([_logical(x).name for x in span[::2]],['tools.mcp__clikernel__py']*3)
test_eq(is_clean(span),[])

title: codexdojo
text:
Template dialog
A live capture can be curated without replaying the whole thread. pick_turns selects clikernel code exactly, falling back to prefix matching, while pick_calls can select any supported nested tool by name and arguments.

Building the review dialog
mk_template adds the synthetic user prompt and short framing messages around already selected native tool pairs. Disabling tool truncation preserves every receipt byte-for-byte for rebuilding.


source

mk_template
def mk_template(
    picked, # Native custom call/result pairs
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
A template dialog with native tool output left untruncated



tdlg = mk_template(mini, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
back = dlg2items(tdlg)
call = first(x for x in back if x.get('type')=='custom_tool_call')
test_eq(parse_exec(call['input']).arguments['code'], 'dojo_start()')

The packaged dialog and store must agree, since the store is compiled from the dialog. Read that reviewed artifact through the same conversion path and reject it if its calls, score, or completion receipt no longer survive the round trip.

packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_items = dlg2items(packaged)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_items)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_items), [])



Compact sample
The package also carries the substantive calls from the completed round as a compact sample session. Startup, kata-control, and scoring calls are omitted; very high token limits retain the captured arguments and results.


source

dojo_sample
def dojo_sample(
    src
):
The completed dojo’s substantive calls rendered as a compact sample session



sample = dojo_sample(packaged_items)
test('doc(find_msgs, view_dlg)', sample, in_)
test('```python', sample, in_)
for omitted in ('dojo_start()', 'dojo_score(', '# kata', '%cd '): assert omitted not in sample
len(sample)

11137


Regenerate the packaged sample after replacing the reviewed Codex template.

sample_path = Path(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'codexdojo_sample.md')
sample_path.write_text(dojo_sample(packaged_items))
sample_path

title: codexdojo
text:
Template store
The store keeps native Responses items plus the clean-round completion id, dojo version, and documented-tool state. It is package data, compiled from the canonical dialog by dojobuild and shipped with the code, so updating llmdojo updates the template with nothing per-user to rebuild.
save_template writes native items and the metadata needed to replay them: completion id, dojo version, and documented-tool state.
It checks the native items with is_clean before writing either store file. build_template uses this same check after converting the edited dialog.


source

save_template
def save_template(
    items, # Curated native template items
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Check the template and write it with its metadata to the store


load_template reads that pair of files without converting the items through another representation.


source

load_template
def load_template(
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
The stored native items and metadata



store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(dlg2items(tdlg),store)
stored,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta,dict(cid='ab12',v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(dojo_cid(stored),'ab12')

build_template is the reverse review path: convert an edited dialog to native items, regenerate ids, and update the store.


source

build_template
def build_template(
    src, # Path to a template dialog
    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
Convert a reviewed template dialog back into the native store



review = store/'review.ipynb'
write_ipynb(tdlg,review)
rebuilt = store/'rebuilt'
build_template(review,rebuilt)
test_eq(dojo_cid(load_template(rebuilt)[0]),'ab12')

title: codexdojo
text:
Launching
Creating a dojo session starts a Codex thread, injects the native template, registers its completion receipt, and seeds the documented-tool state. Appending performs the same injection at the tail of an existing thread after compaction.

Starting a thread
prep_dojo creates a persisted Codex thread, injects a freshly re-id’d copy of the template, registers its completion, and seeds the matching documentation receipts.


source

prep_dojo
async def prep_dojo(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project to start in; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home, primarily for tests
):
Create a thread containing the template and return its id




Refreshing after compaction
append_dojo appends a fresh copy of the worked round to an existing thread and changes only its synthetic prompt to explain why the exercise is repeating.


source

append_dojo
async def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to append to; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
Append the template to an existing thread and return its id


append_dojo is the post-compaction repair. Native compaction replaces the worked history with a summary, so appending restores the demonstrations at the tail and merges their documented-tool state. Re-salting ids makes repeated repairs safe.
The app-server integration runs against an isolated CODEX_HOME, with no model turn: prepare the round and read the thread back as a dialog:

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    home,proj = Path(td),Path(td)/'project'
    proj.mkdir()
    sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
    back = thread2dlg(sid,home,mx=None)
    assert any(m.msg_type=='prompt' and m.content==TMPL_PROMPT for m in back.messages)
    test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])



Compacting with the DSL
Native Codex compaction is encrypted and needs a model turn; llmsurgery.oai.compact_session instead writes a readable compact-DSL document straight into the rollout, offline. compact_dojo chains the two steps — dsl-compact the thread with earlier rounds stripped out of the document, then append a fresh round — so codexdojo -c resumes a session that is both short and re-demonstrated:
The DSL compact should carry the conversation’s work, not its warm-up: the fresh round appended afterwards supersedes any earlier one. As on the Claude side, a round occupies whole user turns, so strip_dojo chunks the items with the shared _turns and drops the turns that dealt a round; compact_session’s strip hook applies it before anything is compacted. A thread holding nothing but rounds is compacted whole rather than emptied.


source

strip_dojo
def strip_dojo(
    items, # Responses items in conversation order
):
Copy of items without the user turns that dealt a round (bare dojo_start())


_strip guards the compaction: when stripping would leave nothing to compact, the round stays:

work = custom_turn('What season is it?', 'tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.')
played = custom_turn('Play the round.', 'tools.mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'), '== llmdojo ==', 'Underway.')
test_eq(strip_dojo(work+played+work), work+work)
test_eq(_strip(played), played)
[item_txt(x) for x in _strip(work+played) if x.get('type')=='message']

['What season is it?', 'Winter.']




source

compact_dojo
async def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Thread id to compact; newest thread for the project if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    codex_home:NoneType=None, # Alternate Codex home
):
Synthetically compact a thread with the compact DSL (previous dojo rounds removed first), then append the template round; returns its id


The same isolated app-server setup drives the offline compaction end to end: prepare the round, append real work through the app server, then compact_dojo:

home = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
proj = home/'project'
proj.mkdir()
sid = await prep_dojo(proj,store,home)
work = custom_turn('What season is it?','tools.mcp__clikernel__py',dict(code='season()'),'winter','Winter.')
async with codex_client(home) as codex: await codex.append_thread(sid,work)
test_eq(await compact_dojo(sid,proj,store,home), sid)

The compact document keeps the real work and drops the dealt round. Codex records fresh context items at resume, ahead of the injected round. The compacted thread still gates clean:

prior,new = split_compaction(load_rollout(sid,home))
body = item_txt(prior[-1])
assert 'dojo_start()' not in body
test('season()', body, in_)
assert any(item_txt(o)==APPEND_PROMPT for o in new)
test_eq(is_clean(active_items(load_rollout(sid,home))),[])
shutil.rmtree(home)



Command line
A call_parse CLI mirroring claudedojo’s (the capitalized params declare the short flags: Resume → -r, Compact → -c): every mode prepares a thread and then execs codex resume on it, with standing arguments from launch_config('codex') (the codex_args list in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/codexdojo/config.toml) and anything the launcher doesn’t recognize forwarded via nested=True. The id comes right after resume, so a stray forwarded token lands in codex’s optional prompt slot rather than stealing the session id; forwarded flag values still need --flag=value form, and the fresh-launch path rejects a stray sess loudly. --sid prints the prepared id and exits. Store builds live in dojobuild.


source

main
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Thread id; the project's newest where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing thread after compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the thread with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared thread id instead of launching codex
    capture:bool=False, # Run a clean round in a bare Codex child and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing thread already played (`capture_current`)
):
Prepare a Codex thread opening with the worked round and launch codex resume on it; template maintenance is dojobuild

title: codexdojo
text:
Rebuilding
Run codexdojo --capture to start a clean dojo round in a separate scratch project and write the accepted round to the local template store. The command uses the same packaged capture prompt as Claude, delivered through the scratch project’s AGENTS.md. It also writes template.ipynb beside the store for review. Curate that dialog with reply2dlg and dlg2reply, then rebuild the stores with dojobuild --codex (and --claude). Use --current when the source thread already completed a clean round.

title: claudesub
text:
claudesub starts a headless claude -p process to work from the parent’s conversation. It gives the child a compact document instead of the full transcript. The document uses llmsurgery’s compaction format to retain decisions and evidence with fewer tokens.
The child runs in its own process with its own clikernel kernel. This differs from Claude Code subagents that share the parent’s kernel in this setup. It also avoids giving a fork the parent’s full context to read on each turn.
Launch the child through a background Bash call or a Monitor. You can read its progress and resume it with an answer after it reports a blocker. This module supports Claude Code. It combines fastclaude.session, llmsurgery.ant.prepare_compaction, and the dojo completion registry.
from fastcore.test import *
import shutil, tempfile

title: claudesub
text:
The parent session
parent_sid reads CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID from the launching process’s environment. In the tested interactive sessions, subagents, and headless children, this ID matches the transcript filename. The function raises if the variable is unset or the transcript doesn’t exist. It never guesses which conversation to compact.
The child skips the practice round using a dojo completion ID. dojo_cid selects the newest receipt for the current tooling version. If none exists, play a clean round in the parent before building the child command.


source

dojo_cid
def dojo_cid():
Return the newest completion ID for this dojo version, or None.




source

parent_sid
def parent_sid(
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
):
Return the launching session ID. Raise if it is unset or has no transcript.



os.environ['CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID'] = 'not-a-session'
test_fail(parent_sid, contains='not-a-session')
del os.environ['CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID']
test_fail(parent_sid, contains='CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID')


cid = dojo_cid()
assert cid is None or len(cid)==4
cid

title: claudesub
text:
The child session
prepare_compaction renders the parent’s conversation as a compact document. It returns a compaction boundary, a summary, and three records for the visible /compact exchange. prep_sub saves these five records under a new session ID.
The child session stays in the parent’s project. A headless resume looks for its transcript there. Claude loads the history after the compaction boundary. The child starts with the compact document and any context the harness adds at launch, without a copy of the full parent transcript.
We’ll check the records using a synthetic parent:


source

prep_sub
def prep_sub(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Parent session id; `parent_sid()` if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
):
Write a session holding only the parent’s compacted history, returning its id for the child to resume



mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
turns = tool_turn('Which module handles retries?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code="rg('retry', 'src')"),
    'src/api.py:12:def with_retry(', 'Retries live in src/api.py.', cwd=mproj)
psid = save_sess(turns, cwd=mproj)
csid = prep_sub(psid, mproj)
child = load_sess(csid, mproj)
test_ne(csid, psid)
test_eq(child[0].subtype, 'compact_boundary')
assert child[1].isCompactSummary and 'retry' in rec_txt(child[1])
test_eq({r.sessionId for r in child}, {csid})
[r.type for r in child]

['system', 'user', 'user', 'user', 'user']

title: claudesub
text:
The protocol and the command
sub_cmd passes the child’s standing instructions through --append-system-prompt, separate from its task directive. These instructions don’t become a conversation turn. Every child uses the same protocol with its chosen dojo completion ID.
The protocol explains the child’s private kernel and receipt-based bootstrap. If blocked, the child must stop and report what it needs rather than wait for an answer. The parent can then resume it. Resuming restarts the child’s kernel, though its conversation remains. The child must finish independent work before stopping and leave a report the parent can use without reading the transcript.
Standing arguments come from launch_config('claude'). The caller’s extra flags follow them.


source

sub_cmd
def sub_cmd(
    directive, # The child's task
    sid, # Session id for the child to resume
    cid:NoneType=None, # Dojo completion id to hand the child; `dojo_cid()` if None
    extra:tuple=(), # Further `claude` arguments, after the standing ones from `launch_config`
):
Build a headless resume command with streaming JSON output. Require a completion ID.



argv = sub_cmd('Summarize src/api.py', csid, cid='ab12', extra=['--model=haiku'])
test_eq(argv[:3], ['claude', '-p', 'Summarize src/api.py'])
assert f'--resume={csid}' in argv and argv[-1]=='--model=haiku'
assert "dojo_start('ab12')" in argv[argv.index('--append-system-prompt')+1]
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = tempfile.mkdtemp()
test_fail(lambda: sub_cmd('x', csid), contains='play one in the parent session')
del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
argv[3:6]

['--resume=683e782a-7b9e-4824-a03d-29bd569be4b1',
 '--output-format=stream-json',
 '--verbose']

title: claudesub
text:
Running the child
run_sub prints the child’s visible text as it arrives. With a background Bash call, this output goes to the task’s file. A Monitor can show each line as an event. quiet=True suppresses progress text and prints the final report instead.
The footer identifies the child session, turn count, and cost. The function returns the result event. It raises if the child exits without a result.


source

run_sub
def run_sub(
    argv, # The child command, from `sub_cmd`
    quiet:bool=False, # Print only the final report and footer, not the child's text as it arrives?
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Directory the child runs in; the current directory if None
):
Run the child, streaming its text, and return its result event


This acceptance test asks about a fact from the synthetic parent’s history. It runs a real model and costs money. Its eval: false flag excludes it from normal notebook execution.

res = run_sub(sub_cmd('From the history only: which file holds the retries? Reply in one line.', csid, extra=['--model=haiku']), cwd=mproj)
assert 'api.py' in res['result']

title: claudesub
text:
The command line
Run claudesub 'directive' to start a child. Use claudesub -r <child-sid> 'answer' to continue one that stopped for help. The resumed child keeps its conversation context.
The CLI uses call_parse(nested=True) to forward unknown arguments to claude. Write them as --flag=value, such as --model=haiku or --max-turns=20. A failed result makes the CLI exit nonzero. Background task notifications can report that failure.


source

main

    directive:str, # The child's task
    Resume:str=None, # A child session id to continue with `directive` as its next prompt, instead of spawning from this session
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared child session id instead of launching
    Quiet:bool=False, # Print only the child's final report, not its progress text
    cwd:str=None, # Project directory to work from, for the parent lookup, the child session, and the child itself; the current directory if None
):
Start or resume a headless Claude child and print its progress and result.
